A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same transformers-on-pixels study. Their text, equations, tables, figures and complete appendices support reliable comparison despite renaming and substantial reorganization.

before.justification: Sections 5–6 and Appendices A–E report original classification, self-supervised learning, image-generation, depth-estimation and diagnostic experiments.

after.justification: Sections 4–5 retain original empirical results, while Appendices F–H add dictionary-embedding, downsizing and token-grouping experiments.

M1.justification: The core architecture remains unchanged under the PiT-to-ViT/1 or DiT/1 renaming. Appendix F adds an auxiliary dictionary-based variant that replaces direct pixel projection with channel-specific intensity embeddings, concatenation and an optional projection. This is a limited input-encoding extension.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate CIFAR-100, ImageNet, Oxford-102-Flower, NYU-v2 and the texture-versus-shape benchmark. Flower classification and depth estimation move from v1 Appendix C into v2's main text. The new experiments vary representations and preprocessing within existing ImageNet classification coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix H/Table 9 adds evaluated FH and SLIC tokenization alternatives against standard patchification. Figure 3 adds actual DiT-L/2 samples alongside the pixel model, whereas v1 displays only pixel-model samples. The main quantitative comparator families otherwise remain.

E3.justification: v2 adds supervised ViT-L configurations, the NYU-v2 RAE metric and a patch-size-16 condition in Figure 2b. New experiments introduce bicubic-versus-single-pixel preprocessing controls and grouping-specific settings, including an FH cap of 225 tokens and 400 training epochs versus the standard 300. Existing principal training recipes remain.

E4.justification: New Appendices F–H substantially extend the diagnostic evidence: they test dictionary versus linear pixel embeddings, whether results depend on locality introduced by resizing, and whether FH/SLIC grouping improves on patches, including SLIC iteration sensitivity. Earlier attention, permutation, shape-bias, learning-rate and extended-training analyses are retained.

E5.justification: v2 Figure 3 newly states that generation seeds are fixed across the compared models. This adds seed-control information, without establishing repeated training runs or uncertainty estimation. Neither version reports confidence intervals, error bars or significance tests.

E6.justification: v2 adds substantial results, including ImageNet ViT-L/1 versus ViT-L/2 accuracy of 76.9 versus 75.6, NYU-v2 RAE of 0.74 versus 0.78, dictionary accuracy of 76.6 versus the retained 76.1, and downsizing/grouping results in Tables 8–9. Figure 2b is replaced, with its pixel endpoint changing from 80.3 to 81.8; v1's unspecified fixed resolution prevents interpreting this as a same-setting gain. Most earlier tabulated results remain unchanged.

T1.justification: v2 Section 3 corrects the RGB vocabulary count from v1's 255^3 to 256^3, and the corresponding patch count from 255^(3p^2) to 256^(3p^2), for channel values spanning 0–255. The Transformer equations remain equivalent; no theorem or proof is added.

C1.justification: The central claim that locality is unnecessary for effective Transformer architectures remains. The introduction narrows v1's statement that translation equivariance is indispensable to the claim that jointly removing locality and location equivariance is not yet feasible. Both versions retain the computational-practicality qualification.

C2.justification: v2 clarifies location equivariance through weight sharing and drops the MAE-specific interpretation that the pixel model's advantage grows with model size. Appendices F–H add explanations involving intensity-order assumptions, locality-agnostic representations and the shortcomings of irregular grouping. The principal computational and coverage limitations remain.

D1.justification: v2 newly specifies the flower-training recipe, depth-training reference, dictionary embedding dimensions, downsizing procedure and FH implementation/parameters. Figure 2b now states a 64×64 input size, which v1 leaves unspecified. Most existing hyperparameters simply move into Appendix A, while v1's explicit ImageNet global-average-pooling statement is omitted.

R1.justification: v2 adds positioning around PixelTransformer by Tulsiani and Gupta and flexible/grouped tokens from Zhang and Maire, Ma et al. and Deng et al., plus references supporting segmentation and depth-training details. Karpathy et al. and Rombach et al. references disappear. The main positioning relative to iGPT and Perceiver remains.

P1.justification: The narrative is extensively revised: PiT terminology becomes ViT/1 or DiT/1, related work moves from Section 2 to Section 6, implementation details move into Appendix A, and existing flower/depth experiments enter the main discussion. Paragraphs, captions and section framing are rewritten throughout.

P2.justification: The document adopts a substantially different ICLR layout. Table 3 consolidates classification and depth results into four panels, Figure 3 becomes paired generation grids, Figure 2 is redrawn and expanded, and Tables 7–9 are added. Existing appendix plots are resized and relabeled.

improvement.justification: Table 8 directly tests a previously unexamined source of locality in resizing, while Figure 3's matched comparisons make generation quality easier to assess. Additional implementation details and prior-work discussion also improve clarity. These strengthen an already supported central finding, with a small reproducibility tradeoff from omitting the explicit ImageNet pooling detail.
